# All cognitive science data in one coherent framework

::: {.lead}
The Behaverse Data Model (BDM) defines how the data of a cognitive science study (including behavior, physiology, and everything needed to interpret it) should be named, organized, and described, so that it can be understood and reused by other researchers, integrated into data catalogs for large-scale studies, and processed automatically by software. The goal is not merely to save time, but to accelerate research and to make possible studies that no single dataset could support.
:::
:::

::: {.bdm-story}
More and more research data is being openly shared. Unfortunately, finding a dataset does not guarantee it is usable. Across datasets, file formats, folder layouts, variable names, and units typically differ, and the information needed to make sense of the data is often incomplete or scattered across multiple sources. [Why BDM](why/index.qmd) documents these problems and examines what current standards do and do not cover.

BDM addresses these problems by defining the data concepts a study involves (e.g., trials, stimuli, responses, options, instructions, agents) along with the variables that describe them, the units and values those variables may take, and where each belongs in the dataset. [Concepts](concepts/index.qmd) explains this framework and shows what a BDM dataset looks like; the [Specification](spec/index.qmd) documents every table, field, and convention in detail.

The definitions are published as versioned, machine-readable schemas, so a dataset that follows them can be validated automatically, combined with other datasets, and analyzed with software written for BDM rather than for a single study. The [Guides](guides/index.qmd) show how to organize an existing dataset, describe it, and store questionnaire and event data; the [Glossary](glossary/index.qmd) defines every term BDM uses.

BDM is developed openly and continues to evolve. The [roadmap](roadmap.qmd) describes what is planned next; questions and proposals are welcome in the [discussions](https://github.com/orgs/behaverse/discussions).
:::


::: {.bdm-proof}
Builds on [BIDS](https://bids.neuroimaging.io/), [xAPI](https://xapi.com/), [schema.org](https://schema.org), [CSVW](https://www.w3.org/TR/tabular-data-primer/), and tidy-data principles · Schemas published at [behaverse/schemas](https://behaverse.org/schemas) · Developed openly [on GitHub](https://github.com/behaverse/data-model)


BDM is part of a larger ecosystem of projects called [Behaverse](https://behaverse.org/), developed by the [xCIT](https://xcit.org/) research group at the University of Luxembourg.

:::
